The stability redesign. JDownloader's dark theme no longer fights the application it lives in — every fragile mechanism from the v2 line has been replaced with an official API, a ground-truth signal, or an empirically verified flow.

## Theming: official FlatLaf API instead of jar patching

- The `#161616` Carbon dark chrome now comes from FlatLaf's official `registerCustomDefaultsSource` API: the container registers its own colour file (`/opt/JDownloader/flatlaf-defaults/FlatDarkLaf.properties`) inside JD's JVM at runtime.
- JD's `flatlaf.jar` stays **stock**. The old mechanism (patching the jar + rewriting its SHA-256 in `flatlaf.dep.json`) is deleted entirely — JD's integrity check is always satisfied, and **a JD self-update can no longer reset the theme**.
- The colour values themselves are unchanged — same monochrome Carbon dark, same light progress fill with inverted percent text.
- Upgrades from v2.x need no action: an existing patched jar keeps working until JD's next self-update replaces it with the stock jar, at which point the new mechanism simply takes over.

## First start: silent headless pre-install, zero dialogs

- On a fresh install the whole JDownloader install chain now runs **headless first** — where no GUI exists, no forced installer dialog can appear. The FlatLaf theme extension is pre-requested in JD's update registry (`flatlaf-themes`), so it installs together with the core.
- The GUI then starts with everything already in place: **the first frame is dark, with zero dialogs** — no more minutes of a black WebUI hiding an installer dialog cascade.
- Fail-safe: if the headless phase cannot settle within 15 minutes, the container falls back to the classic GUI installer (dialogs auto-confirmed by the agent, as before).
- Existing installs that are missing the theme extension are healed automatically the same way (the request is re-seeded until the extension is present).

## Honest READY + ground truth everywhere

- The `JDOWNLOADER IS READY` banner fires only when the agent inside JD's JVM confirms the expected look-and-feel is **actually applied** — never from proxy signals like open ports or files on disk.
- If the theme cannot be verified within 10 minutes, the log says so honestly (`JDOWNLOADER IS UP (theme NOT verified)`) including the likely cause when the theme extension never installed (e.g. a blocked design download).
- The theme healer watches the applied look-and-feel (not disk artifacts), only acts after READY, and is rate-limited to 3 polite restarts per hour — it can heal after weeks of uptime yet can never become a restart loop.
- A revision canary logs JD's exact core build on every launch, so drift after a self-update is diagnosable from the container log.

## Process management

- The launcher loop follows JD's self-update relaunches by **PID** (ground truth from the in-JVM agent) with a grace window and pgrep fallback — a second instance on the same `/config` can no longer be spawned by a mis-detected relaunch.
- Repeated fast crashes back off exponentially instead of hammering a 5-second restart loop.

## New: `JD_SELFUPDATE` (opt-in freeze)

- `JD_SELFUPDATE=false` disables JD's periodic self-update checks for a frozen-appliance setup. Default stays `true` — the same update channel delivers the hoster plugins, which go stale within weeks and break downloads. The first install (and the theme extension install) always use the updater regardless.

## Verification

Every architectural claim in this release was verified empirically before shipping: the FlatLaf API signatures against the library's official signature file, the headless install behaviour and the extension pre-request in four CI experiments on real JDownloader installs, the full diff by an adversarial 18-agent review (three confirmed findings fixed pre-release), and the complete first-start and heal flows on a real Unraid box.
